chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "The hand of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, is above the head of the ruler, fluttering with mercy; so when he is just in his judgment, Allah entrusts him to Himself."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence for a ruler who judges justly according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), the metaphor of God's hand 'fluttering' (turafifu) above the ruler signifies a continuous, active bestowal of mercy contingent upon judicial integrity. This concept is central to Shia political theology, illustrating that the judge's authority is not absolute but delegated, and failure to uphold justice results in divine abandonment (kalahu Allah ila nafsih), a principle often linked to the verse 'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.'
